title: Cargo cults building landing tracks

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that on islands in French Polynesia, in the South Pacific, groups he calls cargo cults built landing strips, presumably for some alien craft they expected to come back, an idea he says comes from their own myths. A researcher and author, Peter Levenda, tells a similar story but places it more broadly on South Pacific islands in the early 20th century, where planes would land, and he does not mention alien craft. Another researcher, Jason Simosa, repeats the story as he heard it from Levenda, describing a tribe in a remote part of French Polynesia, though he admits he is not sure of the geography. It gets told as an example of how people may build rituals around visitors who arrive from the sky.
